What Happened to Poltergeist's JoBeth Williams?

Discover what happened to JoBeth Williams, the star of 'Poltergeist'. From Hollywood horror icon to respected TV actress, explore Williams' fascinating career journey. Learn how she adapted to industry changes and continues to shine in Hollywood.

22 October 2024 · RewindZone Archive

JoBeth Williams was a big star in the 1980s. She scared us in Poltergeist and made us think in The Big Chill. But then, something changed. Let's look at what happened to this talented actress.

Early Days in Acting

JoBeth Williams started her acting journey in Texas. Born in 1948, she loved theater from a young age. After college, she moved to New York to chase her dreams.

"I remember my first audition in New York," Williams once shared. "I was so nervous, but the moment I started reading, I felt at home."

She began with small TV roles and commercials. These jobs helped her learn the ropes of the industry.

Breaking into Movies

Advertisement

Williams' film career took off in the late 1970s and early 1980s. Here are some of her early roles:

  • Kramer vs. Kramer (1979): She played Dustin Hoffman's girlfriend in this Oscar-winning drama.
  • Stir Crazy (1980): Williams appeared in this funny movie with Gene Wilder and Richard Pryor.

"Those early roles taught me so much," Williams said. "I was working with some of the best in the business."

JoBeth Williams' Breakout Roles: A Closer Look

Diane Freeling in Poltergeist (1982)

In Poltergeist, Williams played Diane Freeling, a suburban mom whose life turns upside down when ghosts invade her home.

Character Traits:

  • Loving and protective mother
  • Initially carefree and playful
  • Becomes fiercely determined and brave

Key Moments:

  • Diane's wonder at the paranormal events, sliding across the kitchen floor
  • Her terror when her daughter Carol Anne is taken
  • Her courage in entering the otherworld to rescue Carol Anne

"Diane starts as a typical mom, but she becomes a hero, she'll do anything to save her child." Williams once said.

Diane's journey from a regular mom to a ghost-fighting warrior made her relatable and inspiring. Williams brought warmth and strength to the role, making Diane more than just a screaming victim in a horror movie.

Karen in The Big Chill (1983)

In The Big Chill, Williams portrayed Karen, a former free spirit now living a conventional life.

Character Traits:

  • Dissatisfied with her current life
  • Nostalgic for her younger, more idealistic days
  • Conflicted between duty and desire

Key Moments:

  • Karen's wistful reminiscing about the past
  • Her flirtation with Sam (Tom Berenger), revealing her discontent
  • Her decision to remain with her husband, showing her complexity

"Karen is at a crossroads, she's wondering if she made the right choices in life." Williams explained.

Williams brought depth to Karen, showing her inner struggle between the life she has and the life she once imagined. Her performance captured the film's theme of lost idealism and the challenges of growing older.

Impact of These Roles

These two roles showcased Williams' range as an actress. In Poltergeist, she demonstrated her ability to carry a big-budget thriller. In The Big Chill, she proved she could hold her own in an ensemble drama.

"Those roles were so different," Williams reflected. "They let me show what I could do as an actress."

Together, Diane and Karen established Williams as a versatile actress capable of both action-packed scenes and nuanced emotional performances. These roles set the stage for her career and remain her most memorable characters to this day.

The Big Roles Keep Coming

Advertisement

For a while, Williams was everywhere:

  • Teachers (1984): She acted with Nick Nolte in this school story.
  • American Dreamer (1984): Williams was the star of this funny romance.

She was even on TV in The Day After (1983), a big show about nuclear war.

Signs of Change

In the late 1980s and early 1990s, things started to shift. Williams was still working, but the roles were different:

  • Wyatt Earp (1994): She played Bessie Earp, a smaller role in this big Western.
  • Poltergeist III (1988): She didn't come back for this sequel.

"The industry changes fast, you have to change with it."

Why the Big Roles Stopped

So, what happened? A few things might explain it:

  • Age: Hollywood can be tough on actresses as they get older.
  • Changing tastes: The kinds of movies Williams was known for became less popular.
  • Family life: Williams had kids in the late 1980s, which might have affected her choices.
  • Bad luck: Sometimes, actors just don't get the big parts, even if they're talented.

Moving to TV

As big movie roles became less common, Williams found a new home on TV:

  • Chantilly Lace: JoBeth Williams portrayed Hannah, one of three long-time friends who reunite annually for a weekend retreat.
  • Frasier: She guest-starred and got an Emmy nomination.
  • Dexter: She had a recurring role in this popular crime show.
  • Private Practice: She played "Bizzy," a main character's mom.

"TV gave me a chance to play interesting characters," Williams said. "I'm grateful for that."

Behind the Camera

Williams also tried something new: directing. She made a short film called On Hope in 1994. It even got an Oscar nomination!

Still in the Game

Today, Williams keeps working. She's been in recent shows like Your Honor (2020-2021). She also helps other actors as part of SAG-AFTRA, a big actors' union.

"I'm still here, still working, that's what matters to me."

What Really Happened?

So, what happened to JoBeth Williams? She didn't disappear. She adapted. When big movie roles got scarce, she found new ways to use her talent. She moved to TV, tried directing, and kept acting in smaller roles.

Williams might not be a big movie star anymore. But she's still a working actress after 40 years in Hollywood. In a tough business, that's a big win.

Today, new fans still discover Williams in Poltergeist or The Big Chill. But for her, those are just parts of a long, successful career that's still going strong.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Is JoBeth Williams still acting? A: Yes, Williams is still active in the industry. She's appeared in recent TV shows like Your Honor (2020-2021).

Q: Why didn't JoBeth Williams star in more big movies after Poltergeist? A: While Williams continued acting, changes in Hollywood, including ageism and shifting audience tastes, may have affected her access to major film roles.

Q: What is JoBeth Williams' most famous role? A: Williams is best known for playing Diane Freeling in the 1982 horror classic Poltergeist.

Q: Has JoBeth Williams won any awards? A: While she hasn't won major awards, Williams has been nominated for Emmys and Golden Globes for her performances in The Big Chill, Adam, and Frasier.

Q: Did JoBeth Williams do anything besides acting? A: Yes, Williams has also worked as a director. Her short film On Hope (1994) was nominated for an Academy Award.
